verdict.rationale: Asana documents its own developer sandbox, a temporary Asana domain with limited users, which gives a separate place to test API and agent work instead of using a production workspace. The evidence is a single line, and its documented limits (temporary, limited users) leave the depth of isolation unclear. The deprecation-header testing and read-only MCP tools are adjacent features and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: explicit statement that sandbox data is isolated from production, how to provision it and how long it lasts, whether MCP and agents can target the sandbox, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: A developer sandbox is a temporary Asana domain with limited users.
